uaac30c45b3: Creating a fw file that supports authentication code programming
u8ea252f16a: Authentication codes can only be programmed if the corresponding fw programming file supports it. The steps for creating a fw file that supports authentication code programming are shown in ⟦1⟧Creating a fw file that supports authentication code programming⟦/1⟧:
uba735445e6: Open the ⟦1⟧isd_config.ini⟦/1⟧ file in the download directory of the SDK project;
u10524e4d74: Add the ⟦3⟧AUTH_CODE=1;⟦/3⟧ configuration item to the ⟦2⟧[SYS_CFG_PARAM]⟦/2⟧ section of the ⟦1⟧isd_config.ini⟦/1⟧ file, then save the file;
u8f46bbd9ee: Double-click the ⟦1⟧download.bat⟦/1⟧ script in the download directory to run it;
uc1971f3efc: This regenerates the ⟦1⟧jl_isd.fw⟦/1⟧ file with support for authentication code programming.
u57bb62343b: The ⟦1⟧isd_config.ini⟦/1⟧ file in the SDK may be generated by a preprocessing tool. So if you modify ⟦2⟧isd_config.ini⟦/2⟧ directly and then click Build (instead of double-clicking ⟦3⟧download.bat⟦/3⟧), your changes may be overwritten by a new ⟦4⟧isd_config.ini⟦/4⟧ file generated by the preprocessing tool.
u6b8dec007f: Some SDKs may generate ⟦2⟧isd_config.ini⟦/2⟧ by preprocessing ⟦1⟧isd_config_rule.c⟦/1⟧. If you find that your modified ⟦3⟧isd_config.ini⟦/3⟧ is reverted after you build the SDK, check whether this is the cause. If so, modify ⟦4⟧isd_config_rule.c⟦/4⟧ directly.

uba39dda364: Programming Bluetooth addresses into the target chip
u2b323cf270: Bluetooth addresses are programmed in increasing order, starting from the lowest address of the range configured in the programming options. The programmer programs the Bluetooth address into the target chip at the same time as the chip firmware.
ub383010b24: For example, if the Bluetooth address range is set to ⟦1⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 : 01- 00: 00 : 00 : FF: FF : FF⟦/1⟧, the Bluetooth address of the 1st chip programmed successfully is ⟦2⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 :01⟦/2⟧, that of the 2nd chip is ⟦3⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 :02⟦/3⟧, and so on. After all addresses in the set range have been programmed, the programmer reports "Address overflow" (地址溢出) and can no longer program firmware. Bluetooth addresses are unique: each chip is programmed with a different Bluetooth address.
u561b0e0e16: When the Bluetooth address auto-increment programming feature is configured, each chip is programmed with a Bluetooth address within the specified range. In the SDK, the Bluetooth address can be read through the corresponding function interface and appended to the Bluetooth name in a specified format, so that the Bluetooth name auto-increments with the Bluetooth address and each Bluetooth name is unique (⟦1⟧if you are not sure how to implement this in the SDK code, consult Jieli technical support⟦/1⟧).
udeb046f5ac: For example, if the Bluetooth address auto-increment range configured when updating the programming file is ⟦1⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 :01 - 00: 00 : 00 : FF : FF :FF⟦/1⟧, the Bluetooth address of the 1st chip programmed successfully is ⟦2⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 :01⟦/2⟧, that of the 2nd chip is ⟦3⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 :02⟦/3⟧, and so on;
u1dae8c1e4d: For example, if the Bluetooth name prefix set in the SDK is ⟦1⟧AC897N_Main⟦/1⟧ and the ⟦2⟧Bluetooth name format⟦/2⟧ is ⟦3⟧Bluetooth name prefix + last 8 digits of the address; ⟦4⟧after this is implemented in the SDK code, the Bluetooth name for Bluetooth address⟦/4⟧ 00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 :01 is AC897N_Main_00000001, ⟦5⟧the Bluetooth name for Bluetooth address⟦/5⟧ 00: 00 : 00 :00 :00 :02 is AC897N_Main_00000002, ⟦6⟧and so on. You can define other Bluetooth name formats⟦/6⟧ and implement them in the SDK code⟦/3⟧ to auto-increment the Bluetooth name according to the Bluetooth address.
